vision_features.image_context: A close-up image of a single broad, oval-to-heart-shaped leaf being held in a human hand. The leaf is the primary organ visible, showing its upper (adaxial) surface. Fine short hairs are visible along the leaf margins and veins. A partial second leaf is visible at the right edge. The background is blurred green vegetation.
vision_features.abnormalities: 1. Scattered small-to-medium spots distributed across the entire upper leaf surface, most concentrated in the upper-left quadrant and along the midrib area. Each spot has: a central body of dark reddish-brown to deep maroon color, approximately 2–5 mm in diameter, roughly circular to slightly angular in shape; surrounded by a distinct bright yellow-green to yellow halo approximately 1–3 mm wide around the dark center, creating a 'bullseye' appearance. The spots are dry-looking, slightly sunken relative to surrounding tissue. No raised surface structures are visible on the upper surface. Approximately 20–30 individual spots are countable across the leaf. 2. A larger, more irregular affected zone on the left side of the leaf (near the left lobe/margin), approximately 30–40 mm long and 10–15 mm wide, elongated and somewhat angular, following the area between veins. This zone shows confluent dark brown to tan-brown dry tissue with surrounding yellowed tissue, formed by multiple spots merging together. 3. Smaller, less-developed spots toward the lower-right portion of the leaf are primarily yellow-green halos with only a tiny dark central point, suggesting earlier-stage development of the same type of marking.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery or dusty coating of any color is visible on either leaf surface. 2. No visible raised bumps, pustules, or blister-like structures on the upper leaf surface. 3. No large-scale uniform yellowing of the entire leaf blade — the background leaf tissue remains medium green. 4. No visible distortion, curling, or wilting of the leaf margins or blade.
vision_features.summary: The leaf displays numerous small, discrete spots scattered across the upper surface, each consisting of a dark reddish-brown to maroon dry center surrounded by a bright yellow-green halo, giving a characteristic 'bullseye' appearance. Spots range from pinpoint-sized early-stage marks (yellow halo only) to fully developed marks of 5–8 mm total diameter. The left side of the leaf shows a more severely affected zone where multiple spots have merged into a larger area of dry, tan-to-brown tissue. The most striking feature is the consistent two-tone pattern of each mark: a dark maroon center with a vivid yellow-green border, distributed throughout the leaf surface.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Phytophthora, Sudden death syndrome, White Mold, Anthracnose, Brown Stem Rot, Charcoal Rot, Herbicide injury, Fungicide injury, Late season frost damage, Lightning damage
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. Diaporthe complex (stem canker), Fusarium root rot and wilt, Pythium seedling blight and root rot, Rhizoctonia seedling blight and root rot, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Charcoal rot, Herbicide injury, Early season frost damage, Insect and mite injury
────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. angular leaf lesions with yellow halos
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into large dead areas; older lesion centers may fall out, giving leaves a tattered appearance.
Diaporthe: Characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems for pod and stem blight, and sunken gray-brown stem cankers with reddish margins near nodes for stem canker form.
Decision rule  : IF the primary symptoms are angular leaf lesions with distinct yellow halos and tattered leaf appearance, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight; IF the primary symptoms are linear rows of black specks on stems or sunken nodal cankers with reddish margins, THEN suspect Diaporthe.
